conviction_note: I found no proprietary datum on a $101bn name with forty-plus analysts; what I have is a small net-negative lean on the one number that matters (the Q4 net-new Digital Media ARR guide), from two dated facts the wire has reported as governance/product news but not connected to the guide, partly offset by an independent competitive datapoint that cuts the other way - so I sit well inside the 8.8% implied and below the conviction floor, which is the honest signal that my information content is low.

findings.finding: Adobe must guide Q4 net-new Digital Media ARR on this call with the president of the Creativity & Productivity business (David Wadhwani) having resigned effective 2026-09-27 with no named successor in the 8-K, an interim CFO (Steve Day) since June, and a CEO-elect from the enterprise/Digital Experience side who does not take office until 2026-12-01 - i.e. every person who owns or will own that number is either leaving or not yet in post.
findings.why_not_priced: The market priced the headline - ADBE fell ~7% on 2026-09-04 on the succession and Wadhwani's LinkedIn post, and the 5-day run-up is -9.98%. What it priced was 'we lost a CEO candidate', a governance event. The mechanical consequence is different and is not in any preview I found: the Q4 ARR bar is being set by an interim CFO and an outgoing CEO three weeks before the segment head walks and twelve weeks before a new CEO arrives, which is the textbook set-up for a de-risked guide rather than the 'beat-and-raise minimum' the previews say is required. If this were priced the 25-delta skew would not be -15.2 vol points (the most call-bid name in today's universe) and the preview copy would be arguing about who guides the number rather than about generative AI.
findings.independence: The CEO appointment itself is independently reported by CNBC, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/adobe-anil-chakravarthy-ceo.html (2026-09-03); the interim-CFO leg is independently sourced to the June departure of Dan Durn, https://www.cfodive.com/news/adobe-cfo-leadership-gap-marvell-amid-ceo-search-ai/822849/. Note this finding and finding 2 both predict a soft Q4 ARR guide by different mechanisms and different documents - if the guide is fine, both are wrong together.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-06, three weeks before Adobe's Q3 closed (2026-08-28), Adobe shipped 'Adobe for ChatGPT' - 70+ tools spanning Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, Lightroom, Acrobat and Express, usable 'immediately as a guest' with no Creative Cloud subscription - which lands almost entirely in the Q4 guidance window rather than in the reported Q3 quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The launch was covered as a distribution win (Engadget, Seeking Alpha) and the sell-side downgrades that set the bear case pre-date it - Morgan Stanley on 2026-07-21 to Underweight with a $240 target. Nobody has tied it to management's own Q2 framing that Q3 ARR would be 'soft by design as traffic rerouting takes hold', which is exactly what free guest access to the paid app stack for ChatGPT's user base is. The Q3 number was pre-excused; the Q4 guide is where an Aug-6 free-funnel expansion actually shows up, and it is guided cold on this call. If the market had focused on it, the consumer-press framing ('stop giving $55 a month to Adobe') would appear in the previews, and the previews are still arguing generic AI disruption instead.
findings.independence: Independently confirmed and framed as subscription-cannibalising by Windows Central, https://www.windowscentral.com/artificial-intelligence/openai-chatgpt/chatgpt-users-can-now-use-photoshop-for-free-in-the-ai-bot, and by Engadget, https://www.engadget.com/2231088/adobe-new-chatgpt-plugin-brings-70-of-its-tools-to-openai-chatbot/. Shares an outcome (weak Q4 ARR guide) with finding 1 but no document and no mechanism - see the note there.

findings.finding: Figma - the single company the Adobe bear case leans on hardest - guided Q3 2026 revenue to $373.0-375.0m against Q2 actual $370.1m, i.e. 0.8-1.3% sequential growth and ~36% y/y against 48% y/y just delivered, a 12-point one-quarter deceleration guided by the competitor itself.
findings.why_not_priced: The Figma print was read entirely through its headline - '48% growth, third consecutive quarter of acceleration' - and cited that way in the Adobe share-loss narrative. The sequential arithmetic in the same release points the other way and I found no Adobe preview that does it. If the market had done it, the Adobe bear notes issued after 2026-08-05 would be arguing about whether Figma's seat expansion is topping out rather than treating its acceleration as evidence. Small, because it is a guide from a company two quarters public and everyone discounts those, and because Figma's absolute size is not what determines Adobe's ARR.
findings.independence: Figma's own investor page carries the same numbers, https://investor.figma.com/news-events/news/news-details/2026/Figma-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx; separately, Salesforce's 2026-08-26 Q2 FY27 print (cRPO +14%, FY guide raised, stock +18%) says enterprise software demand in the Jun-Aug window did not deteriorate, https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2026/08/26/fy27-q2-earnings/.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider activity: no Form 4 at all since 2026-08-17 despite the stock falling ~10% in five days and hitting near 52-week lows - no buy cluster, no sell cluster. The only 144 since (2026-09-08) is departed CFO Dan Durn, routine.
Activist involvement - nothing on Elliott, Starboard or ValueAct in ADBE; no 13D on file and the 13G/13G-A stream is routine passive.

WARN / restructuring: no Cal-WARN filing, no restructuring charge in the Q2 10-Q, no 8-K. The 'Adobe layoffs 2026' pages that surface are staffing-agency SEO with no primary source, so I dropped the angle rather than cite it.

FX tailwind to ending ARR: EUR/USD sat ~1.16 through August with a three-month high of 1.1710 on 2026-08-20, i.e. roughly flat across the fiscal quarter versus the 2026-06-11 guide - no mechanical translation surprise to size.

Balance-sheet / disclosure tells in the Q2 10-Q: RPO $22.27bn +13% y/y (in line with revenue +13%), deferred revenue $7.25bn, no new risk-factor language, no ASR, $26.78bn buyback authorisation remaining - nothing anomalous.

Adobe pricing pages and generative-credit terms for a Q3 list-price or credit-enforcement change: the only sources with specific 2026 numbers are SEO aggregators contradicting each other, and helpx returned 403. No primary-source pricing event I would rest a size on.
Adobe community forums / Firefly credit backlash - no concentrated Q3 complaint thread that would read as churn.
Semrush: closed 2026-04-28 at $1.9bn / ~$455m ARR, already in the Q2 base at ~$480m and already publicly identified as the reason the 10.2% FY26 ARR target only looks 'maintained'. Priced.
The stock's own base rate: 'down 10 of the last 12 prints' is already the headline of the Benzinga Q3 preview, so it is wire copy, not an edge.
baseline_tension: My net lean is mildly negative and therefore cuts directly against the baseline's -15.2 skew, which is the most call-bid name in the universe and says the market is paying for a relief bounce off a -9.98% five-day run-in; it agrees with the run-up and with the 1-of-7 up-count in the reaction history, and the honest reading is that a -2.0 against an 8.8% implied is a statement that I could not find enough to justify fighting the option market hard in either direction.
